Metropolis is seeking a Staff Machine Learning Engineer to build and scale our demand forecasting and dynamic pricing systems within the Advanced Technology Group. In this highly impactful role, you will design, deploy, and own end-to-end models that forecast demand, capture price-demand relationships, and use causal inference and double ML to create actionable pricing strategies. You will collaborate closely with product, engineering, and business teams to translate complex requirements into scalable machine learning solutions that directly drive key metrics such as revenue, utilization, and customer demand.

- Proven experience owning and leading projects from inception to production, successfully deploying models and driving measurable business impact   

- Solid understanding of causal inference and experimentation, with experience evaluating both short-term and long-term effects using A/B testing, DiD, Bandits and uplift modeling   

- Strong experience in machine learning modeling and statistics, specifically leveraging time series forecasting, probabilistic models, and deep learning models   

- Experience productionizing and supporting end-to-end solutions using forecasting, optimization, and decision-making algorithms   

- Hands-on experience with data pipeline development, including AWS data storage, data transformation, distributed processing with Spark, and workflow orchestration via Airflow. 

- Experience building agentic AI solutions for pricing is highly desirable. 

- Proficient programming skills in Python and SQL. Power user of AI coding tools. 

- Exceptional communication skills with the ability to bridge technical and business domains, influence stakeholders, read academic literature, and formulate concepts using mathematical notation. Ability to explain complex technical topics to non-technical audiences.

title: Research Engineer, Robotics - Roboticist
job_description:
Research Engineer, Robotics - Roboticist

Persons in these roles are expected to work from our offices in Seattle. On-site requirements vary based on position and team. If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter.

Our base salary range is $128,880 - $193,320, and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package. 

Who You Are:

You will own the control stack on our physical robots and the path from simulation to them. This is first and foremost a controls role: you will bring up and tune real-time, torque-level control on arms, multi-fingered hands, bimanual systems and humanoids, make it stable and safe enough that researchers run experiments on hardware every day, and build the interfaces that learned policies plug into. Experience with humanoid whole-body control and with Unitree platforms (G1, H1 and similar) is a strong plus, as humanoid and whole-body work is a growing share of the lab. You will also design and build the hardware the research needs, from end-effectors to test rigs. You will work closely with research scientists and the simulation team so that what is learned in simulation shows up as reliable behaviour on hardware.

Who We Are: 

The Robotics team at Ai2, led by Dieter Fox, uses scalable simulation to study how foundation models scale and generalize for robotics. We focus on manipulation, humanoid and whole-body control, large-scale simulated training, sim-to-real transfer, robot foundation models and skill learning. We publish at CoRL, ICRA, RSS, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR and ICML, and everything we build is open source.

Your Next Challenge:

- Build and own the real-time control stack: joint, impedance, operational-space and torque control on torque-controlled arms, hands and humanoids, with motion planning, safety layers and the interfaces that learned policies plug into, across embodiments.

- Bring up, tune and stabilize whole-body controllers for humanoids and bimanual systems: QP-based or MPC-based whole-body control, state estimation (IMU, encoders, force/torque), contact handling and fall or fault recovery, and the sim-to-real transfer of learned locomotion and loco-manipulation policies.

- Lead the setup, calibration, maintenance and tuning of our robots: arms, grippers, multi-fingered hands, humanoids, cameras and tactile sensors, across single-arm, bimanual, mobile and legged platforms.

- Diagnose stability, latency and contact problems across hardware, firmware, control and learned policy, using system identification and dynamics models to turn algorithms into reliable real-world behaviour.

- Design and build the hardware the lab needs: end-effectors, fingertips, sensor mounts, fixtures and test rigs, from CAD through 3D printing or machining, including integrating cameras, tactile sensors and hands.

- Build the runtime and tooling around the robots: teleoperation and data collection, logging, monitoring, deployment and operator-facing tools, so the platform scales across robots, tasks and people.

- Contribute to open-source releases and publications.

What You’ll Need:

Minimum Qualifications: 

- Master’s with 3+ years of experience, or PhD, in robotics, control or a related field. Strong candidates with a bachelor’s and 3+ years of industry experience are also considered.

- Controls: you have implemented and tuned real-time controllers (joint, impedance, operational-space or torque control) on physical robots, with a solid grounding in rigid-body dynamics, control theory, stability analysis and system identification. You can explain why a controller went unstable and fix it.

- Whole-body and floating-base control: you understand floating-base dynamics, contact constraints and inverse dynamics, and have worked with at least one of QP-based whole-body control, operational-space control or MPC, on hardware or in a high-fidelity simulator.

- Manipulation: substantial hands-on experience with real-robot manipulation, including bring-up, calibration and control of arms with grippers or hands.

- System design: you have designed robot software systems end to end (control loops at 500 Hz to 1 kHz, state estimation, data flow, and the interfaces between planning, perception and learning) and can reason about latency, reliability and failure modes. Strong Python; solid real-time C++.

- Mechanical design: you have designed and built hardware that was used on a real robot, such as end-effectors, mounts, fixtures or rigs. CAD required (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape or similar), with design-for-manufacturing experience for 3D printing or machining.

- Robot learning: you have trained or deployed learned policies (imitation learning, RL or VLA) on real robots, and are comfortable with PyTorch and at least one simulation ecosystem (Isaac Lab, MuJoCo or similar).

- Debugging across the full stack, from perception through control to hardware, and clear communication with a structured, systems-oriented approach.

Preferred Qualifications: 

- Strong plus: humanoid whole-body control on hardware, including locomotion, loco-manipulation, balance and contact-rich tasks, and hands-on experience bringing up and deploying on Unitree platforms (G1, H1 or similar) or comparable humanoids.

- Depth in control theory: Lyapunov and passivity-based methods, contact-stable and compliant control, dynamical-systems approaches to motion generation, and reduced-order models (centroidal dynamics, SRBD, LIPM), with experience applying them on hardware.

- Sim-to-real for whole-body policies: training RL locomotion or loco-manipulation policies in GPU-accelerated simulators (Isaac Lab, MuJoCo Warp) and getting them to run stably on a real humanoid, including domain randomization, actuator modelling and safety wrappers.

- Whole-body state estimation and sensor fusion (IMU, joint encoders, force/torque, contact estimation, Kalman filtering).

- Experience with bimanual systems, multi-fingered hands or tactile sensing.

- Teleoperation systems (VR, leader-follower arms, hand and body tracking, whole-body retargeting) and large-scale data collection.

- Robotics middleware and infrastructure: ROS 2, DDS or Zenoh, real-time Linux, containerization, CI/CD.

- Hand-eye and multi-camera calibration, depth sensing and 3D perception on hardware.

- Open-source contributions or publications at robotics venues (CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, Humanoids).

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

- Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time. 

- The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations. 

- The ability to observe details at close range.

- Can work under deadlines.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

title: AI Compiler and Performance Engineer

AI Compiler and Performance Engineer

DESCRIPTION

Job Title: Software Engineer, AI Inference Platform

Company: ElastixAI, Inc.

Location: Seattle, WA (Hybrid - 3 days/week in office)




ABOUT ELASTIXAI

ElastixAI is an early-stage startup on a mission to reinvent AI inference infrastructure from the ground up. We’re building a next-generation inference platform that delivers unprecedented efficiency by tightly integrating machine learning, software stack, and custom hardware. Our philosophy is simple: the best performance comes from holistic co-design, where every layer, from model architecture to kernels to silicon, works in harmony. If you’re excited about pushing AI performance to physical limits, and about shaping the future of large-scale inference, we’d love to meet you.




ROLE SUMMARY

We are looking for a deeply technical AI Compiler & Performance Engineer who thrives at the intersection of ML, compilers, and hardware. In this role, you will design how LLM operations decompose into highly efficient proprietary kernel primitives, optimize execution pipelines, and co-develop abstractions with our hardware and ML teams. This is not a “typical” compiler role, it’s a chance to rethink the entire AI compute stack. At ElastixAI, if improving inference efficiency requires inventing new quantization schemes, rethinking graph-level optimizations, or modifying the hardware ISA, we do it. You’ll have end-to-end ownership to explore radically new ideas and make them real.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Break down LLM and transformer workloads into fine-grained primitives tailored to our proprietary compute hardware.

 - Design and implement IR transformations, graph optimizations, kernel lowering, and code generation for novel hardware architectures.

 - Collaborate with ML researchers to co-design algorithmic optimizations that yield real end-to-end performance gains.

 - Work closely with hardware architects to refine microarchitectural features, instruction sets, memory hierarchies, and execution models.

 - Build performance models, profiling tools, and benchmarking frameworks to identify bottlenecks and guide design decisions.

 - Prototype and validate improvements across the entire stack — from PyTorch/XLA-level passes to custom kernel implementations.

 - Contribute to shaping the overall system architecture of a first-of-its-kind inference engine.




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

 - Deep experience building compilers, optimizing kernels, or working with ML frameworks at a systems level.

 - Strong proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Python and C++.

 - Strong understanding of one or more of the following:

Research Engineer, Robotics: Physics Simulation and Sim-to-Real

Who You Are:

You are a simulation engineer who makes physics behave. You have written contact and constraint solvers yourself. When a stack jitters, a grasp slips, an object tunnels through a finger or a gripper linkage explodes, you can tell whether the cause is the timestep, constraint softness, the friction model, the joint formulation or the asset itself, and you fix the root cause rather than adding damping until the problem goes away.

You also know that a stable simulator is not the same as a correct one. You treat logged data from real robots as ground truth. You replay the same motion in simulation, look at the residuals, and close the gap with physics you can explain rather than with magic numbers. You want simulation that a robot foundation model can train on at scale, that never blows up at step ten million, and that behaves like the real world when the policy gets there.

Who We Are: 

Ai2’s Robotics team is led by Dieter Fox. We develop scalable simulation domains to study how robot foundation models scale and generalize, and we build robots that are broadly competent in the real world.

Simulation is central to that mission. We train and evaluate policies across MuJoCo, Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab on Newton, and other GPU simulators, and we deploy them on real bimanual and single-arm manipulators. Whether simulated data is worth anything depends on two things: the simulator must be stable enough to run at scale, and close enough to reality that what is learned there transfers. This role owns both.

Our focus areas include manipulation, large-scale training in simulated environments, sim-to-real transfer, robot foundation models and skill learning. We publish at CoRL, ICRA and RSS, as well as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR and ICML, and we release our models, data and tools openly.

We work closely with other teams across Ai2 and with the University of Washington, only 1.5 miles away.

Your Next Challenge:

The needs below are competencies, not a checklist. If you match many of them but not all, we encourage you to apply.

Stability: Make the Simulator Robust at Scale

- Design, implement and improve contact, friction and constraint solvers: complementarity and soft-constraint formulations, pyramidal versus elliptic friction cones, warm-starting, iteration counts and tolerances.

- Find and remove the failure modes that break large-scale training:

- Jitter in resting contact.

- Interpenetration and tunnelling.

- Energy gain.

- Constraint drift in closed kinematic chains.

- Instability under stiff joint drives.

- Non-determinism across runs and GPUs.

- Make articulated robots and closed loops stable and accurate across MuJoCo, Newton and PhysX: parallel grippers, mimic and coupled joints, tendons. Contribute fixes upstream to those open-source engines.

- Choose integrators, timesteps and substeps with evidence. Show how results change with dt, find where a scene stops converging, and quantify the trade-off between accuracy and throughput for GPU-batched training across thousands of environments.

- Build stress and regression tests for physics: long-horizon rollouts, randomized scenes, extreme parameters and contact-rich edge cases, with failures caught before they reach a training run.

- Make assets simulation-ready: collision geometry, inertial properties, joint limits and contact settings that are stable by construction, consistent across URDF, MJCF and OpenUSD.

Fidelity: Bring Simulated Behaviour Closer to Real

- Fit simulation models to logged hardware data: joint friction (Coulomb, viscous, Stribeck), armature and reflected inertia, payload mass and CoM, actuator drive gains, and latency. Identify what the simulator is missing rather than absorbing it into other parameters.

- Calibrate contact behaviour (stiffness, damping, friction, contact dimensionality, compliance) against recorded pushes, slides, grasps and handovers, so objects slip, stick and settle in simulation as they do on the table.

- Keep the same robot consistent across simulators: one source of truth for frames, masses and contact settings, with MuJoCo, Newton and PhysX agreeing to within millimetres, and every remaining gap explained.

- Own a sim-to-real correlation suite that runs like a test suite:

- Replay recorded trajectories in every simulator.

- Report per-joint RMS, onset lag, velocity profiles and contact-force error against thresholds set in advance.

- Catch regressions whenever a solver, asset or parameter changes.

- Turn measured uncertainty into domain-randomisation ranges for policy training, and measure whether a policy’s real-world success tracks its success in the calibrated simulator.

- Write a model card for each robot and scene: every parameter, where it came from and how much to trust it.

What You’ll Need:

Minimum Qualifications: 

- PhD in robotics, mechanical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer graphics or a related field, or a Masters + 3 years of experience. Exceptional candidates with a bachelor’s degree and 3+ years of relevant industry experience are also welcome to apply.

- Demonstrated depth in rigid-body dynamics and constrained multibody systems: articulations (reduced and maximal coordinates), contact and friction modelling, and numerical integration of stiff systems.

Research Engineer, Climate Modeling

Persons in these roles are expected to work from our offices in Seattle. On-site requirements vary based on position and team. If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter.

Our base salary range is $146,880 - $220,320 and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package.

Who You Are:

We seek a Research Engineer for a new three-year project to develop an AI-powered physics-informed hybrid climate model trained on historical data that is capable of multidecadal forecasts that are more accurate than the current state of the art. We’re looking for someone passionate about improving the quality, efficiency and accessibility of climate models with AI and modern software engineering.  

This position is supported by a grant with a current period of performance ending September 22, 2029. Continuation of the position beyond that date depends on renewal, extension, or identification of additional funding. Ai2 will make reasonable efforts to notify the employee if funding for the position is expected to end.

Who We Are: 

Ai2’s Climate Modeling team is an international pioneer in using machine learning (ML) methodologies to improve on current physics-based climate models.  Our fast, accurate autoregressive open-source emulator, ACE, stably reproduces the climate and weather extremes of an existing climate model or a reanalysis. We have coupled ACE to a ML ocean model, trained it to  realistically account  for changing CO2 concentrations, and downscaled (super-resolved) ACE outputs from their 100 km native scale to to km-scale detail. Our tight-knit team of scientists and software engineers works closely with leading physics-based climate modeling centers to obtain unique training and testing data and get expert feedback on our progress. We collaborate with other leading research groups doing related AI work.

Your Next Challenge:

Physically-based climate models discretize equations representing individual time-evolving processes like clouds, rain, wind, land and sea-ice, and ocean currents on a computational grid.  Some processes (e.g. clouds) are less reliably encoded than others (e.g. winds).  Hence such climate models have biases in representing present-day climate and produce an undesirably large range of projections of future climate change for a given human-caused change in CO2 or other climate forcings.  Current AI-based climate models reduce present-day climate bias, but don’t generalize well to future climate change.

We are starting a 3-year project funded by google.org  to develop an open source ‘AI-first’ climate model that can demonstrably project future climates more accurately than current physically-based climate models when trained on historical observations by judicious design of the AI to incorporate physical principles that reliably apply in any climate, seen or unseen.   The model should be lightweight and easy for an ML-savvy climate scientist to train and deploy. Our starting point is the Google Research NeuralGCM model, a hybrid ML model that uses a conventional discretization of winds encoded in JAX and learns a column-local representation of all other atmospheric and land processes from historical data. Compared to other AI climate models, NeuralGCM uses ML in a conceptually simpler way and shows somewhat better future-climate generalization skill.   It is an open-weight model but its training pipeline  and documentation need to be adapted for a broader user community.

You will join a small team to develop the desired NeuralGCM+ model and foster its uptake by the climate modeling community.  This includes coupling it to an ML-based ocean model and designing approaches to demonstrably improve its skill in unseen climates.  This position has a three year term; there is potential for longer-term funding if  the NeuralGCM+ project demonstrates exceptional progress.

You'll get to work on:

- Adapting the training pipeline and data needs of NeuralGCM to run efficiently on Google Cloud resources and on NVIDIA GPUs.  Note that NeuralGCM is written in JAX and implemented on TPUs.

- Documenting this training pipeline and distributing code on a GitHub repo.

- Implementing and testing a strategy for coupling NeuralGCM with the chosen ML ocean model.  

- Open-source code development as part of a tightly connected team, including daily meetings, code review, design documents and external collaborators. 

- Develop and present tutorials on NeuralGCM+ to interested user groups.

What You’ll Need:

- 2-4 years of experience building and deploying a relevant ML application in a practical or academic research setting and be fluent in Python and collaborative coding practices.

- A B.Sc. in computer or computational science, atmospheric science or a related geophysical science, or applied mathematics/statistics.

- Experience in developing ML training code for use in a cloud computing environment.

- Demonstrated excellent communications skills.

It's A Bonus If You:

- Have a Ph. D. in computer or computational science, atmospheric science or a related geophysical science, or applied mathematics/statistics, with at least one peer-reviewed first-authored publication or accepted conference paper making extensive use of ML in a physical science setting.

- Have formal training and/or practical experience with physically-based atmospheric, oceanic, or related model development.

- Have experience writing machine learning code in JAX.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.
